doc.title: Howie Shear interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2014

chapter: Jazz as a career and wrap-up
title: Student-run jazz at Fredonia and becoming a bebop player
summary: Rowe and Shear recall Fredonia's student-run jazz ensemble; Shear was an ear player until Eastman.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: It was kind of neat being at Fredonia in the 70s with the jazz band, because we sort of used to complain that there was no faculty and they weren’t teaching it. But I think we also thought it was kind of neat that we had that passion and we ran this thing ourselves you know, and it was a real love affair with the music.

Absolutely, yeah. Yeah I agree. I didn’t quite play — I played in the jazz ensemble at Fredonia, and I played some solos but I was an ear player and I didn’t really know how to play chord changes. I had good ears, and I had good feel, and I understood the sound of the language, but I was kind of not really speaking the language of bebop or hard bop or

— until I got into Eastman and I had the time to pursue it as a major. I was still a classical player here. But yes I agree, having something student-run, it’s like owning your own dog instead of renting one. You really want to take care of it.
